recommendations: Joel R Hayes “When Braydon joined Dell for his summer internship, he wisely searched for a mentor. He found me through the mentor portal and took the initiative to reach out. During our first meeting it was clear that he's not only ambitious, but also talented, inquisitive, and humble. There's no ego with Braydon, only the desires to do great work, challenge himself, be a good teammate, and learn as much as possible. It's evident he approaches problems differently than most people, seeking angles most don't consider. I shared some perspectives I've compiled from nearly 30 years in engineering and to recognize how one experience builds on another throughout your career. In return he shared with me notes from his education, the use of AI in school and life, and what he's learned from his work and studies in different countries. He's more than ready to jump in and do great work. I highly recommend him for roles where there are several degrees of freedom that allow him to bring his enthusiasm and creativity to solve challenging problems.”

projects.title: The Corridor
projects.description: Self-Founded project that taught over 500 youth in the span of 2 years, aged 14-16, the skills and importance of leading in a community and being an effective change-maker. I led and guided a group of like-minded leaders, around my age, to help teach and mentor the afore-mentioned youth to make this project a reality.Throughout the two years we orchestrated workshops and community events , resulting in a final student-led charity drive where we taught The participants of "The Corridor" how to raise money, give strong speeches and how to organize a project effectively. One of the results was a stationary drive and cultural immersion event that was possible by collectively raising over R20 000 which provided 400 youth from a nearby school, UkuKhanya Primary school which was not as fortunate as our school, with stationary to last a full school year. This was my final project alongside many smaller events hosted by "The Corridor" before leaving South Africa to travel and work in Israel, Northern Ireland and now the USA to further progress my education and leadership. The Corridor's torch was passed down from me to the youth of "The Corridor" who still create their own community projects to this day.

activity.title: I am a homebody when it comes to music. I love hearing new songs and exploring different genres but to be honest every morning I cycle to work with the exact same playlist everyday. Its just a habit I cannot break hahah. I do want to hear new songs though and so I solved this problem by writing a prompt for 30 seconds to Sauna to build an app so I can explain what kind of songs I want to hear or I can ask it to find new songs for me that fit my vibe. I think it works pretty well and so I wanted to share ! Will be posting more cool use cases of our product so stay tuned ! https://www.sauna.ai/

I wanted to share an appreciation to everyone I met at the Responsible Technology Youth Power Fund Convening last month. To break bread with my generation, and others, and talk about what makes us human and what the world looks like when we collaborate with people to use technology instead of being governed by it I think we build a really powerful movement that centers people at innovation. As an engineer I always have fallen in love with the idea that tech, and of course AI, is a net positive to the world in many facets. And it takes a lot of people with audacity to build and create discourse of what this collaboration should look like in a meaningful way for people. For me personally , I want to keep building technology that firstly is technically impressive and powerful, but more importantly that encourages people to collaborate and work together because when we put a bunch of clever and high agency people in a room together with a shared mission, then we reach the moon :) I love leading AI Consensus , and I love building with cracked eng and people. I am honoured to live this life coming from Pinetown in South Africa, and there is a whole lot more I want to do in this world so keep watching. Thank you for your support in our mission Responsible Technology Youth Power Fund <3

This morning my AI built a piece of software for itself. Nobody asked it to. This is our biggest feature launch ever: APPS. We're officially declaring war on SaaS 😄 Here's why: Software until now: guess which SaaS fits → buy it → bend your workflow around someone else's buttons Sauna: chat through the problem → artifacts appear (docs, PDFs, HTML) → do it twice → Sauna builds the app, for you AND for itself → the chat stays docked, and both the app and the agent have full context about you, your team, and every other app The agent "presses" its own buttons, so every run gets quicker. It learns from mistakes at scale, and everything about the job lives in a real database instead of an MD file. Example: you need to send a calendly link to a VIP, but you have no free slots. Sauna rebuilds calendly from a template in seconds, decides from context which dates to offer and which internal events could move for someone this important, and ships it as a GUI. If the VIP books over your team sync, Sauna pings the attendees on Slack and moves it. Painfully simple. https://lnkd.in/gGXiH-qZ

Thank you for having me and AI Consensus! This is a spectacular mission to be a part of and our team is more fired up than ever to bring Responsible AI to everyone we can :) Responsible Technology Youth Power Fund a truly exceptional convening and I look forward to doing so much more together. Thank you everyone who made the convention so special!

Wang might be one of the most talked-about people inside Meta right now. But why? Several reports suggest his leadership has become a lightning rod for debate inside Meta’s AI organization. Critics have questioned his relative lack of traditional AI research experience, while others point to internal restructuring, leadership tensions, and Meta’s massive AI investments as reasons for the scrutiny. But this isn’t really about him. It’s about what happens when companies bet billions on AI. Expectations become enormous. Every leadership decision is analyzed. Every delay is criticized. Every reorganization becomes headline news. That’s the reality of leading one of the world’s biggest AI initiatives. Whether Wang ultimately succeeds or not won’t be determined by social media debates. It will be determined by one thing: Can Meta build AI products that create real value for billions of users? In technology, perception changes quickly. Execution lasts much longer. #Meta #AI #ArtificialIntelligence
